newsitem.title: USA: Doomed rocket carried Lockheed satellite.
newsitem.headline: Doomed rocket carried Lockheed satellite.

text.p: Lockheed Martin Corp said it built the navigational satellite that was aboard the Delta rocket that exploded shortly after takeoff here Friday.

Commissioned by the U.S. Air Force, the satellite was built at the company's Missiles and Space facility in Valley Forge, Pa. It was to have been deployed once the rocket reached orbit, according to Lockheed Martin spokesman Eric DeRitis.
He declined to place a value on the satellite, but published reports had said it was worth about $40 million.
The NAVSTAR Block IIR satellite was one of a new generation of U.S. Air Force Global Positioning System satellites.
A spokesman for Boeing Co said a division of his company built the engine of the unmanned Delta II rocket.
McDonnell Douglas Corp built the rocket itself. The rocket was supposed to have launched at 1128 EST/1628 GMT. Witnesses said the explosion occurred at about 1132 EST/1632 GMT. No one was injured.
